lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Sit if you are sitting, help if you are standing. I have bowls to fill and rooms upstairs. What do you need?
lines.direction: Brisk, warm West Country voice; busy hands, practical kindness, no sentimentality.

options.label: Show us the rooms and prices.
How is the town holding up?

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: A room, a hot bowl, and a door that shuts. We will sort out who is staying.
lines.direction: Brisk, warm West Country voice; busy hands, practical kindness, no sentimentality.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: People come in talking about the cold and go out talking about the stew. I can manage one of those problems.
lines.direction: Brisk, warm West Country voice; busy hands, practical kindness, no sentimentality.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Mind your scarf. Wind is getting into everything.
lines.direction: Brisk, warm West Country voice; busy hands, practical kindness, no sentimentality.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: My hearth's the warmest in town again. People keep asking me why. I keep telling them it's the stew.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: You'll want feeding. Sit. I heard what happened on the bridge. I'm not asking, and you're not telling. Not tonight.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Half the town says you've gone soft, and the other half is eating better for it. I know which half I'm in.
